leads.title: HB 1570 - Arkansas ban on puberty blockers, hormone therapy for under 18
leads.documents: Criminalizes/prohibits gender-affirming care for minors; veto, override, and enforcement status relevant to trans visitor healthcare access
leads.detail: Cited as 'HB 1570' passed March 2021, vetoed April 5 by Gov. Asa Hutchinson as 'overbroad' and 'extreme', veto overridden next day; ACLU sued, federal judge blocked enforcement. No URL visible in text.

leads.title: U.S. District Court ruling June 20, 2023 by Judge James M. Moody Jr. striking down HB 1570
leads.documents: Finds trans healthcare ban discriminated against transgender people, violated doctors' rights, state failed to prove experimental-nature claim; shows current rights machinery and irreparable harm finding
leads.detail: Cited as June 20, 2023 ruling by federal judge James M. Moody Jr. who had previously blocked law; AG Tim Griffin and Gov. Sanders vowed appeal. No URL visible.

leads.title: Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals Aug 12, 2025 reversal / United States v. Skrmetti
leads.documents: Allows state to enforce trans youth care ban, citing U.S. Supreme Court ruling in United States v. Skrmetti; documents final enforceability for safety dossier
leads.detail: Cited as 'On August 12, 2025, the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals overturned the lower court's ruling...citing...United States v. Skrmetti.' No URL visible.

leads.title: SB270 / Act 619 bathroom ban - April 11, 2023
leads.documents: Amends 'sexual indecency with a child' to cover trans person using public bathroom/locker room/changing facility matching gender identity while minor present; final version requires intent of 'arousing or gratifying a sexual desire', misdemeanor with sex-offender implications
leads.detail: Cited as SB270 put forth February, became Act 619 April 11, 2023, narrowed to intent standard. No URL visible.

leads.title: Arkansas public school bathroom law signed March 21, 2023 by Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders
leads.documents: Prohibits trans people from using public school bathrooms matching gender; makes Arkansas 4th state with such law after Alabama, Oklahoma, Tennessee
leads.detail: Cited as signed March 21, 2023 by Governor Sarah Huckabee Sanders. No URL visible.

leads.title: Arkansas transgender athlete ban - signed March 25, 2021
leads.documents: Legally bans transgender athletes from sports and athletics; enforcement risk for trans visitors participating in athletics
leads.detail: Cited as Legislature passed March 2021, signed March 25 by Governor of Arkansas effective immediately. No URL visible.

leads.title: Gender-affirming litigation bill - signed March 13, 2023 by Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders
leads.documents: Allows individuals to sue doctors/nurses for gender-affirming care provided as minors, 15 years after turning 18 vs 2-year limit for other care; chills provider availability
leads.detail: Cited as passed March 2023, signed March 13, 2023, effective summer. No URL visible.

leads.title: Arkansas gender-marker rules: 1981 birth certificate law + DFA X descriptor policy
leads.documents: Permits birth certificate amendment upon court order verifying sex reassignment surgery and name change; ID documents available with X since Dec 2010; DFA rescinded X for driver's licences March 2024
leads.detail: Cited as 'Since 1981...' and 'Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration has issued such documentation since December 2010. In March 2024, the DFA rescinded...' No URL visible.

leads.title: Intrastate Commerce Improvement Act (2015) and Arkansas Supreme Court Feb 2017 Fayetteville decision
leads.documents: State law prohibits counties/municipalities from creating protected classes not in state law; used to strike down Fayetteville and render Eureka Springs/Fayetteville LGBTQ employment ordinances unenforced; explains lack of local protection
leads.detail: Cited as Senate passed Feb 9, 2015 24-8-2, House passed Feb 13, 2015 58-21-14-7 present, emergency clause rejected; Supreme Court struck down Fayetteville ordinance Feb 2017. No URL visible.

leads.title: Bostock v. Clayton County (2020), SB 289 healthcare denial law (2021), and hate-crime law status
leads.documents: Bostock provides only statewide sexual orientation/gender identity employment protection; SB 289 allows medical practitioners to cite religious beliefs to deny LGBT patients signed March 26 by Gov. Hutchinson; Arkansas has no bias-penalty hate crime statute and April 2021 watered-down law excludes sexual orientation/gender identity
leads.detail: Cited as Bostock banned discrimination nationwide in 2020; SB 289 passed House and Senate early 2021; Matthew Shepard and James Byrd, Jr. Hate Crimes Prevention Act Oct 2009 covers federally. No URL visible.
